newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Islamic leaders assemble to honour Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Islamic leaders assemble to honour Pakistan.

text.p: Leaders from the Islamic world will hold a special summit meeting in Islamabad on Sunday to honour Pakistan on the golden jubilee of its independence.
But analysts said the absence of some important Arab leaders would make the one-day gathering a low-key affair with more ceremony than substance.

Eleven presidents, four vice-presidents, three crown princes and six prime ministers, four deputy prime ministers and 21 foreign or other ministers will be among the participants of the first ever extraordinary summit of the 54-member Organisation of Islamic Conference (OIC), a Pakistani spokesman said.
But he said no king would come in what is a rare departure from the previous seven summits of the 27-year-old group, which stretches from Africa to Central Asia.
Pakistan officials say the summit would underline the Islamic world's solidarity with Pakistan, which emerged in 1947 at independence and partition of the Indian subcontinent.
The meeting, which will follow a big military parade, will consider a vague one-point agenda on "preparing the Islamic world for the 21st century".

A declaration to be adopted by the conference would refer to problems facing the Moslem world in political, economic and other fields and suggest ways to overcome them, Pakistani spokesman Inamul Haq told a news conference on Saturday.
Among these problems he cited what he called "cultural aggresssion" and "misinformation" directed gainst Islamic countries in the western media.
"We will refer to these problems and suggest ways and means to overcome them," he said.
Also to be mentioned in the declaration would be the Palestinian question and Pakistan's dispute with arch-rival India over the Himalayan region of Kashmir.
Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani, Turkish President Suleyman Demirel and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat will be the most prominent leaders at the summit.
Crown Prince Abdullah of Saudi Arabia will represent King Fahd.
Egypt's President Hosni Mubarak, citing Middle East tension, is staying away, as are Syria's President Hafez al-Assad, Iraqi President Saddam Hussain and King Hussein of Jordan.
Morocco's King Hassan, the current OIC chairman, is also staying away and will only send a message to be read at the meeting's inaugural session.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina of Bangladesh, which seceded from Pakistan in 1971, arrived on Saturday as the only woman leader at the event.
Afghanistan's seat the conference will remain empty following an earlier OIC decision because of rival claims by warring factions there.
But Haq said representatives of the Taleban Islamic movement, which controls more than two-thirds of Afghanistan, and some other Afghans will attend as guests.
He said representatives of an umbrella All Parties Hurriyat (freedom) Conference of groups fighting Indian rule in Kashmir had not arrived because of India's refusal to give them travel documents.
